newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean group to invest $560 mln in natgas scheme.
newsitem.headline: Chilean group to invest $560 mln in natgas scheme.

text.p: A group headed by Chilean power utility Tocopilla is planning to invest $560 million in building a natural gas pipeline from northern Argentina to Chile across the Atacama Desert, said a top official.

The consortium will spend $330 million on building the duct from gasfields in the Argentine province of Salta to the port of Tocopilla, said Luis Hormazabal, development manager at Electroandina, the new name for recently privatized Tocopilla.
"Another $230 million will be invested (by Electroandina) in building two combined cycle units at the Tocopilla plant with a capacity of 460 megawatts," Hormazabal told Reuters.
Outline details of the scheme were announced last month.
The group, known as Norgas, is one of three rival projects battling to build energy projects to fuel the fast-growing mining industry in Chile's arid north.
Analysts have said there is only room for one scheme.
Electricity giant Endesa and U.S. energy firm CMS Energy are also planning a gas pipeline.
The third group, led by generator Chilgener, is building power plants in Salta and will bring electricity to Chile using a transmission line across the Andes.
The Norgas duct will have a minimum capacity of four million cubic meters a day and a maximum of seven million, he said.
"Finding buyers for four million will be enough to guarantee the project," said Hormazabal.
Tocopilla's new power plants will use 2.2 million cubic meters and the rest will be sold to customers including other power generators, mines and industrial firms in the region.
The company needs to sign up one power generator, requiring at least a million cubic meters a day, and another non-electric customer for the project to be viable, he said.
Hormazabal said Tocopilla has already held talks with power utility Edelnor, fertilizer-maker Soquimich and explosives firm Enaex.
The project should supply gas to Tocopilla by September 1999, six months later than the scheme planned by Endesa.
Tocopilla, which used to belong to state copper producer Codelco, is the largest generator in northern Chile.
The firm supplies power to the Chuquicamata pit, Codelco's largest division, and to the recently built El Abra mine.

Codelco sold a 51 percent stake in the firm last year for $178 million to a group including Spanish firm Iberola Energia de Espana, Belgian companies Powerfin SA and Tractebel and Chilean company Enagas SA.
Codelco owns 34 percent but plans to sell its shareholding on the bourse this year. The rest is held by workers.
